editorial.headline: Used Motorcycles: Nationally Open, Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Retailing used motorcycles is nationally open to PMA ownership, but Bali’s permanent risk-based moratorium blocks a PMA registration there today.
editorial.body:
This activity covers the retail sale of used motorcycles, extending to motorised bicycles and mopeds. Its focus is firmly on the retail transaction: bringing pre-owned two-wheeled vehicles to market for buyers. The definition is concise, yet it establishes a clear operating centre for the enterprise. The relevant business is the one retailing a used machine, whether the vehicle is described as a motorcycle, a motorised bicycle or a moped. That precision gives the activity a distinct commercial identity.

Registration is available at each stated scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. This gives the classification a wide stated range of enterprise size, from Mikro through Besar, without changing the underlying activity. A small retail operation and a larger company can therefore look to the same activity description when their work is the retail trade described in the record. The scale list is an eligibility signal; the substance remains the retailing of used motorcycles, motorised bicycles and mopeds.

At the national level, the PMA status is TERBUKA and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. In ordinary terms, the national record permits this activity to be fully foreign owned. That is a significant starting point, but it is not a Bali registration permission. Bali records the activity as blocked for PMA registration. The reason given turns on its OSS risk position at the Besar scale: every scope is classified Low or Medium-Low risk. In Bali, that risk character is decisive because the province’s stated moratorium captures all Low and Medium-Low risk activities for PMA.

The Bali measure is described as permanent and island-wide. Its result is direct: a foreigner cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today, despite the national 100% ceiling. For a founder reading the code, the right conclusion is not that the national allowance is misleading, but that it operates at a different level from the provincial registration outcome. The national position is open; the Bali route is currently closed for PMA registration. The national ceiling therefore cannot be read as a Bali registration permission.
